suggested_title: Mason Muir - MD Student at WashU School of Medicine
prospect_notes: Mason Muir is an MD student at Washington University School of Medicine (Class of 2028), originally from Moline, IL. He completed his undergraduate degree in Molecular Biology and Genetics at Cornell University. He serves as an Admissions Liaison for WashU Medicine, helping prospective students learn about the program. His interests include discussing resources at WashU, places to live in St. Louis, St. Louis food scene, Forest Park, and the WashU student/faculty community feel. He also discusses the experience of having a partner/family in medical school. LinkedIn profile confirms his Cornell University Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics background and current enrollment at WashU School of Medicine.

suggested_title: Clara Liu - MD/PhD Student (MSTP) at WashU School of Medicine
prospect_notes: Clara Liu (full name Jingxian 'Clara' Liu) is an MD/PhD student in Washington University's Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP), enrolled in the Computational and Systems Biology PhD program under advisor Li Ding, PhD. She grew up in Beijing, China and studied biology and computer science at Cornell University, graduating in 2019. She enrolled in the WashU MSTP in 2019. Her research focuses on multi-omic investigation of tumor clonal evolution, studying how tumor cells accumulate genetic alterations during malignant transformation and interact with the tumor microenvironment. She co-authored a 2024 Nature paper on tumour evolution and microenvironment interactions in 2D and 3D space (Nature, 634(8036):1178-86).

_enrichment.title: MD/PhD Student (MSTP), Computational and Systems Biology

suggested_title: Virginia Hsu - MD/PhD Student (MSTP) at WashU School of Medicine
prospect_notes: Virginia Hsu is an MD/PhD student in Washington University's Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP), enrolled in the Neurosciences PhD program under advisor Shin-ichiro Imai, MD, PhD. She completed her undergraduate degree at Cornell University, graduating in December 2016 (confirmed via Raguso Lab alumni page at Cornell). Her research focuses on NAD+ metabolism and aging: brain NAD+ levels decrease during aging, and she studies how boosting cellular NAD+ via precursor administration ameliorates age-dependent pathologies and metabolic changes. She is affiliated with the Imai Lab in the Department of Developmental Biology at WashU Medicine.

suggested_title: Amith Punyala - MD/PhD Student (MSTP) at WashU School of Medicine
prospect_notes: Amith Punyala is an MD/PhD student in Washington University's Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP), enrolled in the Molecular Microbiology and Microbial Pathogenesis PhD program under advisor Sean P. J. Whelan, PhD (Department Chair). He graduated from Cornell University in 2019 (Twitter confirms 'Cornell University 19') with a background in Chemistry and Chemical Biology, receiving an undergraduate award from Cornell's Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology in 2016-17 and contributing to published research on Wnt/PCP signaling at the Weill Institute for Cell and Molecular Biology. His current MSTP research focuses on determining host factors necessary for the entry and replication of Thogotoviruses and Rhabdoviruses in the Whelan virology lab.

_enrichment.title: MD/PhD Student (MSTP), Molecular Microbiology and Microbial Pathogenesis
